history.reason: Begin an executable schema-v3 epoch without inventing live-cycle evidence for schema-v1 promotions.

checkpoint.goal: Maintain nulnul-harness as a verified meta-harness that converts measured failures into independently gated improvements.
checkpoint.milestone: Make measured setup, workflow, activation, and fast-path performance release-blocking and stabilize bounded fast resume.
checkpoint.completion_check: python3 scripts/pack_plugin.py && python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v && python3 plugins/nulnul-harness/skills/nulnul-harness/scripts/check_doc_debt.py .
checkpoint.last_verified: 2026-08-11: Gate v5 replaced historical arm names and the absolute fast-path token ceiling with version-independent champion/candidate comparisons. Four counterbalanced paired rounds gave Navigator v12 4/4 bounded behavior, three comparable pairs, and -18.4% median paired input-token change under the 20% budget. The runner records stage times and bounded tool/read/validator/test counts without raw transcripts; fixed-order and mismatched-pair negative controls fail closed. The 29-file archive matched the plugin, all 79 repository tests and 12 product tests passed, learning and evolution validation passed, document debt was empty, and Release Gate returned 100/100 with release_ready true.
checkpoint.next_action: Observe whether repeated completion-check commands persist now that benchmark telemetry exposes them; add a release guard only after a reproduced candidate improves that count without hurting behavior or paired cost.

navigator.job: Own verified-only resume, explicit checkpoint compatibility, transactional migration, unattended host boundaries, permissions, and final synthesis.

coach.job: Require, convert, and machine-link every reproducible nonpass verdict to bounded feedback and proposals while preserving rejected search knowledge.

gate.job: Independently compare candidates, require machine-verified public-run evidence, and promote, reject, or roll back.

product-builder.job: Implement the smallest complete product change and leave executable verification.

feedback.observed: The continuation benchmark reported context-cost improvement as not established, but the active evolution state did not convert that machine-readable result into Coach feedback or a next proposal.
feedback.expected: Every reproducible rejected, regressed, failed, or not-established verdict becomes bounded feedback and one pending proposal in the same run.
feedback.evidence: evals/benchmarks/setup-baseline/results.json continuation status and this run's preserved candidate decisions.

feedback.observed: Two prior continuation runs completed correctly but used 260119 and 315284 input tokens, so a context-cost improvement was not established.
feedback.expected: Resume a covered task from concise verified state with exact behavior and a lower repeated-run median without expanding permissions.
feedback.evidence: evals/benchmarks/setup-baseline/results.json resume_gate reproduces the baseline and four candidate mechanisms.

feedback.observed: The concise checkpoint stored free-form evidence but could not distinguish verified, failed, and unknown current state before fast resume.
feedback.expected: Only an explicitly verified valid checkpoint may enter fast resume; failed and unknown remain valid diagnostic states.
feedback.evidence: The prior checkpoint schema and validator had no verification-status field or fast-path predicate.

feedback.observed: The learning-loop rule existed in prose, but no check proved that every machine-readable nonpass verdict linked to its feedback and proposal.
feedback.expected: A deterministic validator fails when any rejected, regressed, failed, or not-established verdict lacks both links.
feedback.evidence: The setup benchmark stored nonpass results separately from evolution state and the product test checked no cross-file identity link.

feedback.observed: Projects configured before the concise checkpoint release retained a full-contract session entry and had no verified migration path.
feedback.expected: Upgrade the legacy durable contract in place without inventing verification, losing permission constraints, touching protected host paths, or creating a second writer.
feedback.evidence: The 1.3.0 project and AGENTS templates had no concise checkpoint entry, while 1.3.1 only specified new day-one output.

feedback.observed: Checkpoint schema version 1 represented multiple incompatible shapes and could still be mistaken for the current fast-resume contract.
feedback.expected: New checkpoints use schema version 2, valid version 1 checkpoints remain readable but never fast-resumable, and unknown future versions fail closed.
feedback.evidence: The checkpoint compatibility tests exercise version 1, version 2, and an unsupported future version.

feedback.observed: A result file could omit learning_verdicts entirely and bypass the cross-file learning-loop validator.
feedback.expected: Any measured nonpass requires a learning_verdicts inventory, and both the product check and release gate reject its absence.
feedback.evidence: Negative controls remove learning_verdicts and require both validation surfaces to fail.

feedback.observed: Sequential migration writes could leave a checkpoint and guidance file at different generations when a later replacement failed.
feedback.expected: Prepare every update first and restore every replaced file if any replacement fails.
feedback.evidence: A deterministic second-replacement failure injection verifies that no new checkpoint or partial guidance edit remains.

feedback.observed: A headless Claude Code adopt run read the protected-path rule but still issued two Write calls against existing .claude/agents profiles, then treated the host denials as an acceptable manual follow-up.
feedback.expected: Classify .claude/** as read-only before roster inspection, issue no write tool call against it, and upgrade existing roles only through repository guidance during unattended runs.
feedback.evidence: The first isolated 1.3.3 run recorded both denied Write calls; a fresh patched run exposed the same tools but recorded zero protected-path write calls.

feedback.observed: The Release Gate awarded the Claude adoption weight by trusting a hand-edited passed status without checking the protected-write trace, agent hashes, or validator exits.
feedback.expected: Require a sanitized structured artifact and reject any protected write, changed profile, stale version, missing setup output, or failed check.
feedback.evidence: The previous release_gate.py summed statuses only; its new negative control injects a protected write and fails the gate.

feedback.observed: A generated verified checkpoint stored a prose success description in completion_check, and structural validation still allowed fast resume.
feedback.expected: Store the exact repository command and execute that field successfully before verified fast resume.
feedback.evidence: The observed prose form now fails validation; the shipped runner executed the public E2E checkpoint's exact npm test command with exit code zero.

feedback.observed: The successful Claude adoption rerun loaded a local plugin directory, so it did not prove the documented GitHub marketplace install path.
feedback.expected: Count the adoption case only when the active plugin source is GitHub and its installed version matches the release manifest.
feedback.evidence: The final fresh run used the GitHub marketplace installation at version 1.3.5 with no plugin-dir override.

feedback.observed: Release readiness could remain 100/100 while recorded setup, workflow, or fast-path token and elapsed-time metrics regressed, and activation coverage was four one-shot cases.
feedback.expected: Fail releases on published performance regression and keep a repeated positive, negative, and fast-path activation matrix.
feedback.evidence: The existing release score summed behavior statuses without opening the A/B measurements; the activation runner defaulted to one round across four cases.

feedback.observed: A fresh verified-checkpoint fixture completed correctly but stayed inside its checkpoint and task-file read budget in only 1 of 3 runs.
feedback.expected: All three fresh runs must validate first, avoid full repository discovery, change the requested behavior, and pass the recorded check.
feedback.evidence: evals/benchmarks/activation/results.json preserves the failed baseline, two rejected rules, and the accepted 3-of-3 arm.

feedback.observed: The fast-path gate used a 250000-token absolute ceiling, historical version and arm names, fixed champion-first order, and no stage or tool telemetry; a same-source run exceeded the ceiling and reproduced one forbidden discovery read.
feedback.expected: Use generic champion/candidate evidence, counterbalance arm order, compare only behavior-valid pairs against a relative budget, and retain bounded aggregate telemetry without raw transcripts.
feedback.evidence: The fixed-order 3-pair run failed at 2/3 champion behavior; the counterbalanced 4-pair run exposed one excluded champion pair and three valid cost pairs.

feedback.observed: Fresh fast-path runs still occasionally used repository discovery, while aggregate telemetry also exposed repeated completion-check commands that token-only evidence could not explain.
feedback.expected: Name forbidden discovery commands, keep the completion check on the shipped wrapper, preserve exact behavior, and stay within the paired relative cost budget.
feedback.evidence: The final candidate stayed bounded in 4/4 rounds and improved median paired input by 18.4%; repeated check counts remain measured feedback rather than an unproven release threshold.
